description.narrative:
KRDF's Strategy for 2020-2024 specifies four strategic objectives: 1) Improve skills and capacities of vulnerable groups for better opportunities 2) Improving economic and environmental conditions for vulnerable groups in Kakheti 3) Support vulnerable groups to exercise their human rights 4) Improve KRDF's services, systems and structures, accountability and transparency
Note: The strategy states that it should be implemented in the Kakheti region, however the main part of the activities will be implemented in specific parts of Kakheti, mainly: Akhmeta, Karajala and the Pankisi-valley.

Kakheti Regional Development Foundation, KRDF har inkommit med ett förslag om kärnstöd för att genomföra organisationens strategi för 2020–2024 under perioden juni 2020-december 2022.
Stödet är en fortsättning på det inledande kärnstöd vilket genomförts under perioden från augusti 2019 till och med mars 2020. I det inledande kärnstödet ingick även externt stöd till att utvärdera KRDF:s dåvarande strategi samt att utveckla en ny strategi för 2020–2024. Ambassaden handlade även upp en revision av intern styrning och kontroll under genomförandet av det inledande kärnstödet. KRDF:s respons till revisionen samt tillhörande handlingsplan har godkänts av ambassaden. Genomförande av handlingsplanen ingår i det föreslagna kärnstödet.
KRDF är en georgisk civilsamhällsorganisation som är grundad i, samt bedriver verksamhet i Kakheti och framför allt i Pankisi-dalen i östra Georgien. Pankisi-dalen bebos bland annat av en etnisk minoritetsgrupp, Kister samt flyktingar från Tjetjenien och är en isolerad region med många utmaningar, gällande såväl fattigdom som rättigheter.
KRDF strategi för 2020–2024 innehåller fyra strategiska målområden:
1) Stärka utsatta gruppers kunskap och förmågor för förstärkta möjligheter i samhället. 2) Stärka möjligheterna för utsatta grupper att förbättra sina ekonomiska och samhälleliga förutsättningar i samhället. 3) Stödja utsatta grupper med att åtnjuta mänskliga rättigheter 4) Förbättra KRDF:s service, system, strukturer samt ansvarsutkrävande och transparens.
Sidas finansiering av insatsen uppgår till 6 200 000 SEK och består av såväl direkta kostnader för genomförandet av strategin som kostnader för personal och administration.

Kakheti Regional Development Foundation, KRDF has presented a proposal for core support for implementing the organisation's strategy for 2020-2024, during the period June 2020- December 2022. The proposed contribution is a continuation of the pre-core support which has been implemented during the period from August 2019 until end of March 2020. In the pre-core support external support to KRDF to evaluate their previous strategy and to develop a new strategy for 2020-2024 was included. The Embassy also procured an internal Control audit of KRDF during the pre-core support. KRDF's management response and action plan to the audit has been approved by the Embassy. The implementation of the action plan is included in the proposed core support.
KRDF is a Georgian civil Society organisation which is founded in, and implements most of their work in Kakheti, and in specific in the Pankisi-valley in the Eastern parts of Georgia. The Pankisi-valley is inhabited by the ethnic minority Kist's and refugees from Chechnya and is overall an isolated region with many challenges with regards to both poverty and human rights.
KRDF's Strategy for 2020-2024 constitutes of four Strategic Objectives:
1) Improve skills and capacities of vulnerable groups for better opportunities 2) Improving economic and environmental conditions for vulnerable groups in Kakheti Region 3) Support vulnerable groups to exercise their human rights 4) Improve KRDF’s services, systems and structures, accountability and transparency
The budget proposed by KRDF is after being rounded upwards to 6 200 000 SEK and constitutes of as direct costs for the implementation of the strategy as well as costs for staff and administration.

Achievements of the contribution against the strategic objectives are as follows:
Strategic Objective 1: Improve skills and capacities of vulnerable groups for better opportunities.
For achieving results KRDF provides wide range of courses in different communities through establishing training centers the KRDF calls Community Development Groups (CDG). 5 CDGs have been created (2 in Karajala, 1 in Koreti, 1 in Akmeta, and 1 in Omalo) over the project lifetime. Thus the objective has been achieved only partially as the target indicator was establishment of 10 CDGs.
In 2020, order to ensure that the KRDF offered courses had not been already provided by the other institutions, KRDF conducted a mapping/listing of vocational programs and professional courses. The mapping was done through information and consultation meetings and included online as well as in-person opportunities.
The programs offered by KRDF are designed to better address the needs of local population and prevent the overlap between other programs. KRDF offered free educational and vocational courses in three educational centers (Jokolo, Duisi, Koreti) of Pankisi gorge in 2020. From 2021, the courses were also offered in Karajala. The courses were offered in: Needle Felting Sewing, Culinary, Georgian song, Dance, Pottery, and Knitting, apart of them the educational courses include: History, Computer, English language, Math, Geography, Civic education, Georgian language and Literature, and Art. In 2021 and 2022, career development courses were also offered.
On average, around 300 beneficiaries attended the courses each year. The majority of the students were women and girls. In total, as of June 2023, 270 students attended vocational courses and 420 were involved in the educational courses.
Strategic Objective 2: Improving economic and environmental conditions for vulnerable groups in Kakheti
The overall indicator for the objective states that the number of representatives of vulnerable groups who improved their economic conditions should increase by 20%.
For achieving the result the KRDF designed the grant providers database and conducted the informational campaign for Akhmeta Municipality residents. As a result, more than 86 person were directed to the different grant providers.
Besides the KRDF has disbursed 30 small business grants to the community members (12 small grants in 2020, 10 - in 2021, and 8 - in 2022).
In conjunction with grant distribution and for ensuring that the participants had sufficient skills for managing the grants, subsequent trainings and consultations were offered by KRDF. The business consultations touched upon the subjects of how to better start, manage, and improve business practice. In addition, those who did not receive a grant were provided with consultations on how to better prepare business plans and improve their business ideas in future. There were certain cases, where people were disappointed with KRDF due to being refused to get a grant. To mitigate disappointment, KRDF provided detailed information about the reasons of refusal to everyone that asked about it.
Beneficiaries of the KRDF grant for small business stated that the grant led to various benefits, such as an increase in the number of clients/customers, an increase in income and/or the creation of new sources of income and establishing relationships with people in the area - according to the KRDF mid-term evaluation review.
To sum up, according to the quantitative research within the frames of the mid-term evaluation by DEPA has shown that out of all the surveyed 144 vulnerable beneficiaries (grantees, as well as beneficiaries of educational and vocational courses) approximately 32% have improved economic conditions in the last three years. The rest 68% state that their economic condition has not changed over that period, but importantly, none of the vulnerable respondents have stated that their economic condition has worsened.
Strategic Objective 3: Support vulnerable groups to exercise their human rights
The overall Indicator of the third Strategic Objective was phrased as follows: Vulnerable Groups of two Kakheti Municipalities increased awareness and better exercise their rights, which will be reflected in the number of changes designed by women and men together according to the Georgian legislation (concerning Humans, Childrens and Womens Rights) which are represented in Kist traditional customary law codex.
A working group was created in 2020 with KRDFs support to work on modernization of the customary law. The customary law is a set of rules that has been passed down in a verbal form for generations and has been written and printed in 2017. The Elderly Council (a group of elderly, well-respected man from the community) makes decisions based on these rules when there is any kind of conflict within the community. A substantial part of the Kist population sees the customary law as a main set of rules to obey and recognizes the Elderly Council as decision-makers, even though they have no formal institutional power. In certain cases, if the issue is discussed in customary law, going to the formal law enforcement is not accepted by the community, which can create a fear of isolation. In addition, even if a person has been/is being prosecuted by the state law, the customary law prosecutes them separately and imposes certain sanctions. The customary law involves clauses that are not always in line with the state law. But, because it is still obeyed and used, the working group was created to adapt it so that it considers womens and childrens rights and needs to a bigger extent. For this purpose, the working group included representatives from the Elderly Council, the Womens Council, local active women and KRDF lawyers.
KRDF hired an external consultant who gave recommendations on what should have been changed for Kist customary law to be in line with the state and international law. The recommendations were then thoroughly discussed with the representatives of the working group. After the recommendations package was designed the Council of Elders made their feedback regarding the document and after the final presentation and discussion they agreed to advocate the future changes in customary law codex.
The issue of the customary law is rather sensitive and in certain terms controversial. This has been discussed with KRDF on number of occasions.
Also, Capacity building trainings were organized for the local government representatives for better provide social programs and communication strategies with the ethnic minority representatives, also to better plan and implement the programs for protection of victims of violence.
During the project period KRDF actively provided free legal consultation to 20 persons and legal assistance to 36. KRDFs lawyer cooperated with central government to discuss the issues of 150 individuals living in Pankisi who did not have Georgian Citizenship and thus had limited access to state programs.
KRDFs youth and womens groups actively joining the 16 days campaign against gender based violence in order to raise awareness of the local population in remote areas about the gender equality and gender based violence in general. During the campaign, local women and youth organized film screenings and seminars covering the topics of womens rights and gender equality.
In 2021 the KRDF even introduced a prize for outstanding achievement for gender equality work bearing the name of famous female Georgian writer Barbare Jorjadze. The Jorjadze prize is awarded to womens rights defender in the region. It is crucial that these women are supported and the society is aware of their work, so that the rights of rural women are better promoted. societal stereotypes weakened and more people know women are not only supposed to restrain themselves with domestic labor and child-rearing. The KRDF worked hard to get across the message among target women they can get education, develop professional skills, strive for self-employment and achieve economic independence. During the project implementation period two womens rights defenders were awarded and also the annual conferences were organized for reviewing the statistics about the violence against women and possible ways to better act for preventing DV GBV among the vulnerable communities in Kakheti Region.
Strategic Objective 4: Improve KRDF's services, systems and structures, accountability and transparency
The core support among other things intended to improve KRDFs internal operational and financial systems which was one of the biggest challenges for the organization. KRDF has worked on its internal policy documentation in order to adopt them to the Georgian legislation and international standards. KRDF has improved financial and administrative policies. A number of policy documents have been updated and created by KRDF, including: anti-corruption, child protection, terms of employment, employee code of conduct, personal data protection risk management, accounting, financial handbook, fundraising strategy, labor regulation, procurement. KRDF purchased financial program Balance for better financial follow up. It also tries to introduce modern M&E. However, the M&E system is still very flawed, as the internal documents are not always cohesive and because KRDF does not have a specific person assigned for M&E.
To sum up overall the results achieved as have been described in the DEPA evaluation "KRDF has made a visible impact in three main dimensions: womens livelihoods, infrastructure, and youth. Local women are more aware of their rights, active in the community and empowered through number of capacity building and grant opportunities. When it comes to infrastructure, repaired road, increased water accessibility, new trash bins, and waiting areas have been constructed due to the CDG advocacy initiatives. For youth, the ethnic integration, inter-generational and inter-cultural boding has resulted from youth camps and educational activities".
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
